title: Exact scalar restriction and normalized coefficient cones at one site
statement: Fix a prime l and a scheme T with DiagonalTraceLocalizations l T [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-models]. For normalized Chern data c for E=ULift Q_l [def-sp-tower-class-chern], there exists an exact section-preserving residue Restriction r [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-models] and a Coefficients record for c,r [def-sfb-diagonal-trace-coefficients]. This constructs only data at T, without a scheme morphism or any ordinary or derived direct-image comparison.

source.place: paragraph (1), ordinary scalar restrictions before right derivation

proof.text: Choose the exact residue restriction independently of the Chern data. Choose the unital additive coefficient identification and the pure-tensor root identification for this restriction. These are separate finite constructions; neither produces a completed projection cone.

The scalar equation for r at z=l^(n+1) shows that every level section is killed by l^(n+1). For any additive map from a Z_l-module into this level, write z-a=l^(n+1)b using the p-adic approximation a; additivity and annihilation imply f(zx)=z f(x). Thus every additive sheaf map into a level lifts to a unique discrete-Z_l-linear map.

Apply the lifting result componentwise to the actual ring-limit projection cone followed by coefficientForget inverse, and to the actual root-limit projection cone followed by lineForget inverse. Naturality survives because lifting leaves the additive maps unchanged. Cancelling each inverse followed by its comparison proves both sectionwise projection equations. Package these cones with the finite identifications into Coefficients.

theorem exists_diagonalTraceCoefficientRestriction (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime]
    (T : Scheme.{u}) [DiagonalTraceLocalizations l T]
    (c : Chern l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) T)
    (hc : c.Normalized l (ULift.{u} (Padic l))) :
    ∃ r : Restriction l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) T,
      Nonempty (Coefficients l (ULift.{u} (Padic l)) T c r)
